prediction.likelyOutcome: 7205 Telegraph is likely to prevail on the core liability theory — the site-plan/zoning shortfall is effectively conceded by the Association's own expert, and the undisclosed board conflict of interest undermines any business-judgment defense of the 2015 reallocation. The real fight is over quantification: the two experts bracket the diminution-in-value damages anywhere from roughly $110,000-$145,000 (Association's framing, closer to the actual 12-space reality) to $1.34 million (7205 Telegraph's most favorable framing), with the true number likely landing well below the high end given that actual post-reallocation parking (12 spaces) tracks much closer to the Association's 15-space benchmark than to plaintiff's 5-space worst case. The Association's lien counterclaim for unpaid post-2017 assessments, and the fee-shifting provision, add real but currently unquantifiable exposure/upside on both sides.

outcome.description: After a bench trial the Fairfax County Circuit Court entered judgment for 7205 Telegraph on all four counts, awarding $481,434.84 in lost-rent contract damages, a further $6,296.70 for over-assessments, release of the association's liens, and $324,977.60 in attorney's fees and costs. A Court of Appeals panel affirmed on April 25, 2023; rehearing en banc was granted, and on December 19, 2023 the court lifted the stay and left the judgment affirmed.
outcome.finalNote: Affirmed, including after rehearing en banc.
